messages.author: 09e9d545e0510a59
messages.subject: Skewed segregation and stepwiseqtl problem
parts:
Hi,


I have a couple of problems with QTL mapping in a tomato RIL population (130 individuals) genotyped with sequencing data (GBS and RNAseq) with about 2500 genomic bins:

  1. I have a couple of regions (on different chromosomes) with strongly skewed segregation (probably due to bushy phenotypic selection). One is about 2% genotype B and the other one is about 10% genotype A. That cause me artificial QTLs in a stepwiseqtl analysis. Do you think it will be wise to not using these markers? Do you have other suggestions?
  2. The stepwiseqtl analysis tends sometimes to split a qtl into 2 adjacent qtls. It adds 2 (or more) markers (their names are as the original markers with “1” addition) adjacent to the marker with the highest lod score (I got that from the attribute “lodprofile”). One of them has a zero lod, and the other has a lod similar to the original qtl. That cause 2 adjacent qtls. Any idea why is that happening and if (and how) it can be solved?

I would appreciate any help with these,


Thanks, Itay

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Skewed segregation and stepwiseqtl problem
parts:
>
>
> • I have a couple of regions (on different chromosomes) with strongly skewed segregation (probably due to bushy phenotypic selection). One is about 2% genotype B and the other one is about 10% genotype A. That cause me artificial QTLs in a stepwiseqtl analysis. Do you think it will be wise to not using these markers? Do you have other suggestions?

I wouldn't expect artifactual QTLs; I would expect just low power. But if what you believe that what you're getting are artifacts, I'd trim out the regions.

> • The stepwiseqtl analysis tends sometimes to split a qtl into 2 adjacent qtls. It adds 2 (or more) markers (their names are as the original markers with “1” addition) adjacent to the marker with the highest lod score (I got that from the attribute “lodprofile”). One of them has a zero lod, and the other has a lod similar to the original qtl. That cause 2 adjacent qtls. Any idea why is that happening and if (and how) it can be solved?

I've experienced various problems with tightly linked markers, but I've not tried stepwiseqtl with this sort of marker density. Do you get different results if you perform the stepwise analysis "by hand" using makeqtl() and addqtl()?

karl

messages.author: 09e9d545e0510a59
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Skewed segregation and stepwiseqtl problem
parts:
Thanks Karl!

1. I'm quite sure about the artificial qtl, especially in the 2% area, as only one marker shows a lod score above the threshold (1000 permutations) and it relays on 2-3 individuals. I'll try to trim these are out and see what I get.

2. As I'm running eQTL analysis for entire transcriptome I'm using an automated script so I didn't try "by hand" makeqtl() and addqtl(). However, the script runs automatically makeqtl() and addqt() and write the results into a different file and I find this split phenomenon only in the stepwise analysis.

Itay
